## Summary

There is a low severity vulnerability in Traefik's Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider. With `allowCrossNamespaceResources` disabled (the default), the cross-namespace check on the `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-secret` annotation only runs when a client authentication TLS option is first built: a later Ingress referencing a CA secret already used by another Ingress reuses the shared TLS option without being checked. A user allowed to create Ingresses in one namespace can therefore have a CA secret from another namespace enforced as the client certificate authority of their own routes, bypassing the configured namespace isolation, and learn whether that secret exists and is in use; the secret's contents are not disclosed. The issue was introduced in v3.7.11, when client authentication TLS options started being shared across Ingresses; earlier versions are not affected, and Traefik v2 is not affected since it does not include the Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider.

## Patches

- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v3.7.15
